Report in commit '[PEO-002] report'. Manual pass; open: suite 0.57s, PEO-023 resolved, CPU 99%.

review: rework. The World seam itself is good and is on main; these are concrete changes, not a redesign. 1. The determinism case asserts scent().total() through doctest::Approx, which allows about 145 ULP (+/-0.000277 on a total near 22.2). Both worlds run in one process from one binary, so the result is expected bit-identical, and every neighbouring assertion in the same case (player, turn, each horde position) is already exact. Assert exact equality. 2. total() is a std::accumulate over the whole grid, a lossy summary: two genuinely different fields can share a total, so the case does not test what the brief means by 'same world'. Compare the field cell-wise, or hash it. 3. The brief specifies 100 turns; the test runs 30 with an inline note about sanitizer cost. The suite now sits at 0.15 s against a 500 ms budget, so measure it and restore 100, or change the brief and say why in the report. 4. Build the release preset and a clang build before pushing to main. This series left main red for about 25 minutes because -O3 and clang-18 both reject code the Debug preset accepts; that gap is tooling's fault as much as anyone's and is now its own queue item.

Correction to point 3 of my review: I quoted the suite at 0.15 s, which was measured before this item's own tests were merged in, and the advice that followed was backwards. Measured now: 0.95 s for 25 cases, against the 500 ms budget in AGENTS.md - the suite is over, not under. The four test_world.cpp cases account for 0.82 s of that; the slowest is 'reaching exit advances stage_index' at 0.46 s. So point 3 is replaced: do not restore 100 turns. Bring these cases under budget first - measure with peo_core_tests -d, and note that a World step is a full ScentField sweep, so turns multiply by grid area. Then judge whether 100 turns is affordable at a smaller grid. Points 1, 2 and 4 stand as written.

Weighted-draw movement for the Dead with aggregates and company pull

notes.text: D-007 (see decisions.md) fixes the shape of the draw: weight a candidate cell by pow(scent, k) with a tunable exponent k slightly above 1, never exp(k*scent) — at the 0-500 scale from PEO-026 exp saturates immediately. A power law keys off the ratio between neighbouring cells, so one k stays decisive next to the player and becomes a gentle drift far away, which is the horde-drift behaviour the user asked for. Fold this into the brief when PEO-009 is planned.

items.title: Frontend busy-loops: release build uses ~78% of a CPU core at idle

notes.text: briefed

Severity should be raised S3 -> S2 (work_queue.py set has no --severity flag, so this note is the record of the request; only add takes one). Measured worse than when filed, not better. PEO-002 added a 'dirty' flag so draw() is skipped when nothing changed, but SDL_AppIterate still returns SDL_APP_CONTINUE immediately every iteration (src/app/main.cpp:162-169) and the renderer is created with flags 0 and never gets SDL_SetRenderVSync (:123). The loop is now a pure unthrottled spin with not even a present to pace it, so it saturates a core harder than the ~78% originally filed; the Builder reports ~99%. The fix is unchanged - vsync or a frame cap - but it is now the most user-visible defect in the queue.
Severity raised to S2 with the new set --severity flag; the previous note recorded the request only in prose because the tool could not express it.

items.title: The Dead do not converge within 3 s: scent spreads ~8 cells in 20 s, so distant Dead never move

notes.text: Raised D-007 (scent reach / convergence pacing). Blocked on the pacing answer: the front-radius test in this brief can only pin a number once the target reach is chosen. Technical instrumentation is ready to write behind the decision.

D-007 answered and recorded in decisions.md; briefed. Root cause identified from the code: the ~8-cell reach is the floor flush in scent.cpp (v < floor -> 0.0F, floor 0.001F against a 1.0F deposit); past it the field is exactly zero, strongest_neighbour requires v > best strictly, so distant Dead never move. Fix is dynamic range, not diffusion rate.

Brief corrected: kPlayerScent already exists at src/app/main.cpp:26 as 1.0F, so the unit raises it rather than introducing it. Starting tuning values (diffusion 0.8, decay 0.01, floor 1e-6) are carried over from branch claude/fervent-curie-iqonhg, which reached the same numbers independently; that branch's pinning test asserted only sample > 0.0F against a 1e-6 floor, which passes on the tail crossing rather than a usable scent level, so the tests here assert a strictly decreasing gradient and actual Dead convergence instead.

Re-briefed against measured data. Two corrections to my earlier brief: the acceptance test I wrote was unsatisfiable (at 200 steps the front reaches 45 cells, and I asserted at 62 — sample was exactly 0.0), and diffusion 0.8 is in the oscillatory regime. Verified replacements are in the units. Separately, D-008 now covers the finding that a moving player outruns their own scent entirely, which this item cannot fix.

Do not start this before the wall-absorption item (order 255). That change alters the field's shape, so both the retune constants and the test parameters in these units — which were measured on an open grid with reflecting edges — must be re-derived afterwards. Ask the Architect to re-measure rather than guessing new numbers.
